item.title: Democrats hit a new milestone: 100 women in the House
item.description:
Democrats are projected to win back the U.S. House — and hit a major milestone. For the first time ever, at least 100 Democratic women are expected to serve in the chamber simultaneously. “Women made history because we showed up to vote, and then voted in more than 100 Democratic women to serve in the House,” Rep. Teresa Leger Fernandez of New Mexico, the chair of the Democratic Women’s Caucus, said in a Wednesday statement. She added: “Women have borne the brunt of the Trump administration’s recklessness and Republicans’ extremist agenda, and on Tuesday they made it clear they have had enough.” Elect Democratic Women (EDW), the campaign arm of the House Democratic Women’s Caucus, has had its sights set on achieving that goal since the beginning of the cycle, several House Democratic women told The 19th last year. “We think 100 is a great number. item.title: How Democrats Can Stop the Iran War Now
item.description:
The Great Democratic Crack-Up starts now. That may sound a bit odd, given the party’s historic thrashing of Donald Trump and the Republican Party on Tuesday. Let me explain. For months, the anger and divisions have been bubbling up—the uber-progressive left pushing back against what it views as a feeble and feckless Democratic leadership, the leadership trying to hold things together, and the bundlers in New York and Los Angeles and elsewhere raising oodles of cash . Georgia senator Jon Ossoff reeled in $115 million; Texas’s new Democratic senator James Talarico, $146 million; and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, $38 million—of which she gave $1 million to Democratic Senate contender Abdul El-Sayed. That spending paid off: The Democrats now control the House and the Senate. item.title: South Africans vote in local elections seen as test for embattled ANC
item.description:
Party expected to get less than a third of the vote amid frustration over water outages and power cuts The African National Congress is on course for a bruising result in South Africa’s local elections on Wednesday as voters go to the polls amid deep discontent over water outages, power cuts and crumbling infrastructure. The former liberation movement, which Nelson Mandela led to power in 1994 at the end of apartheid as South Africa’s first black president, is still likely to be the largest party. However, polls show it getting less than a third of the vote, down from 45.6% at the last municipal elections in 2021 and 40.2% in 2024’s national elections . Continue reading...

item.title: House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries declares "America is back"
item.description:
The witness-prep business is about to take off for Washington law firms. As Democrats appear poised to take the gavel, at least in the hearing-happy House of Representatives, the task of helping corporate executives prepare for their turn in the chair — a DC practice known as “murder-boarding” — will be in high demand. item.description:

item.title: What made Haley Stevens turn on El-Sayed? | Judith Levine

item.title: Four oil tankers destroyed in Hormuz after hitting mines, Tehran says
item.description:
Four oil tankers caught fire after hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz, Tehran claimed Wednesday, a day after US President Donald Trump said the United States had launched strikes on Iran. Discussions to end the war between Washington and Tehran via mediators have continued with little sign of diplomatic breakthrough.
